evidence: Log of legally required releases and of releases cleared by legal counsel
Documented restrictions on distributing workpapers and final communications
Requests for records, with the decision and its approver
audit_focus.recommend: Name in the function's methodology who may approve each kind of release of engagement records.
audit_focus.decides: The chief audit executive decides who receives final engagement communications

subtopics.isaca_rule: Must: disclose confidential information only to an authorized party or under a legal or professional duty, by the set route; the CAE must seek required advice before an outside release. Confidentiality never keeps a finding from the board.

exam_traps.trap: The matter is confidential, so the auditor leaves it out of the report to the board.
exam_traps.why: The board is an authorized recipient of results. Leaving out a finding breaks the honesty requirement; sensitivity is managed by restricting distribution.

exam_traps.trap: Confidentiality lets an auditor refuse a disclosure that the law requires.
exam_traps.why: The duty has an explicit exception for legal or professional responsibility, and auditors must make the disclosures that laws and regulations require.

key_terms.definition: A duty set by law, regulation or professional standards that requires a disclosure.
Legal protection that can keep certain communications with lawyers from being disclosed.
The function's rules for who may receive engagement records and who authorizes it.

key_terminologies.Domain II: The second domain of the Global Internal Audit Standards, on ethics and professionalism: Principles 1 to 5 and Standards 1.1 to 5.2.
key_terminologies.Requirement: A part of a standard that uses "must": it is mandatory.
key_terminologies.Consideration for Implementation: A part of a standard that uses "should" (preferred practice) or "may" (an option): not mandatory.
key_terminologies.Chief audit executive (CAE): The person who leads the internal audit function and answers for its quality, ethics and conformance.
key_terminologies.Engagement: One piece of internal audit work with its own objectives and scope.
key_terminologies.Engagement supervisor: The internal auditor who directs an engagement and reviews its work: the chief audit executive or someone they delegate.
key_terminologies.Board: The top governing body that authorizes and oversees internal audit; often the directors as a group, or their audit committee.
key_terminologies.Senior management: The top executives, usually including the chief executive officer, who answer to the board for running the organization.
key_terminologies.Assurance services: Objective assessments against criteria that give stakeholders confidence about governance, risk management and control.
key_terminologies.Advisory services: Advice given at a stakeholder's request, with no assurance and no management responsibility taken on.
key_terminologies.Integrity: Honesty plus the courage to act on the facts, whatever the pressure; the base of the other four ethics principles.
key_terminologies.Professional courage: Communicating truthfully and acting properly in a dilemma or under pressure.
key_terminologies.Discreditable behavior: Conduct that harms trust in the auditor, the organization or the profession, such as lying about a credential.
key_terminologies.Objectivity: Each internal auditor's bias-free way of thinking, which keeps judgments tied to evidence.
key_terminologies.Independence: The internal audit function's freedom to work without bias or interference, secured by reporting directly to the board.
key_terminologies.Impairment to objectivity: A situation, activity or relationship that may bias an auditor's judgment, in fact or in appearance.
key_terminologies.Self-review bias: Reduced critical thinking when an auditor reviews their own earlier work.
key_terminologies.Familiarity bias: Assumptions from past experience that take the place of fresh evidence.
key_terminologies.Conflict of interest: A competing personal or professional interest that could sway an auditor's judgment or seem to.
key_terminologies.Perceived impairment: A situation others would reasonably see as bias, even with no bias in fact.
key_terminologies.Refrain rule: An internal auditor must not assess a specific activity they were previously responsible for; the Standards set no end date.
key_terminologies.12-month presumption: For assurance, objectivity is presumed impaired when the auditor was responsible for the activity in the previous 12 months.
key_terminologies.Safeguard: A step that removes or reduces a threat to objectivity, such as reassignment or outside supervision.
key_terminologies.Designated supervisor: The person named by the chief audit executive to receive an auditor's disclosure of an impairment.
key_terminologies.Competency: What an auditor knows and can do, at the level the job needs.
key_terminologies.Continuing professional development: Ongoing education, training and experience that keep an auditor's competencies current.
key_terminologies.Due professional care: The diligence, judgment and skepticism of a prudent, competent internal auditor; reasonable care, not perfection.
key_terminologies.Professional skepticism: An unbiased, questioning attitude: critically assessing whether information is reliable before relying on it.
key_terminologies.Confidentiality: Keeping information gained at work for work purposes alone, and away from anyone not authorized to have it.
key_terminologies.Methodologies: The chief audit executive's written policies and procedures for how the function does its work.
